metadata.purpose: Validate Scientific Reflow against published results from NSLS2 SIX beamline

reference_paper.title: Magnetically propagating Hund's exciton in van der Waals antiferromagnet NiPS3
reference_paper.authors: He, W., Shen, Y., Wohlfeld, K., Sears, J., Li, J., Pelliciari, J., et al.

metadata.validation_approach: Model experimental setup (Systems A-F with F as pass-through), run gap closure, compare inferred System D properties to published results

validation_strategy.description: We will treat the NiPS3 sample as having PARTIALLY_KNOWN properties (crystal structure known, electronic excitations UNKNOWN), then use gap closure to see if we can infer the exciton energy and dispersion relation from the RIXS measurements.
known_beforehand: Lattice parameters: a=5.812 Å, b=10.07 Å, c=6.632 Å, β=106.98°
Electronic structure: Charge-transfer insulator, bandgap ~1.6 eV
discovered_by_experiment: Dominant interaction: Hund's exchange (~1.4 eV energy offset from double-magnon)
validation_strategy.gap_closure_target: Can we infer the exciton energy (1.47 eV) and Hund's exchange interaction from the RIXS spectral data?
validation_strategy.success_criteria: Gap closure should propose exciton energy within ±10% of published value (1.47 eV ± 0.15 eV = 1.32-1.62 eV range)

Cool sample below TN=155 K to study antiferromagnetic state

experimental_components.description: Van der Waals antiferromagnetic NiPS3 crystal - electronic excitations UNKNOWN

physical_properties.magnetic_order: KNOWN: Antiferromagnetic zigzag chains, TN=155 K

experimental_components.gap_closure_goal: Infer exciton energy and Hund's exchange interaction from RIXS spectral data (sample→detector measurements)

constraints.resonance_condition: Maximum exciton intensity at Ni L3 edge (~853 eV)

experimental_components.notes: THIS IS SYSTEM D - THE KNOWLEDGE GAP. Exciton properties are UNKNOWN and will be inferred from RIXS measurements.

experimental_components.description: Ultra-high-resolution soft X-ray RIXS spectrometer at SIX beamline

physical_properties.energy_resolution: 14 meV at 1000 eV (total), ~17 meV at 853 eV (estimate)

experimental_functions: Measure inelastically scattered X-ray energy (Ef = Ei - ΔE)
Resolve energy loss ΔE with ~17 meV resolution
Detect scattered X-rays at various angles (k-space mapping)
Record RIXS spectra as function of energy loss

measured_observables.primary_observable: RIXS intensity I(Ei, ΔE, k) as function of energy loss ΔE

experimental_components.notes: THIS IS THE CRITICAL MEASUREMENT - RIXS spectra encode exciton energy and dispersion

experimental_components.description: Minimal processing pipeline - RIXS spectra are directly interpretable, no transformation required

pass_through.input_data: I(ΔE) - RIXS energy-loss spectrum from spectrometer

physical_properties.data_format: HDF5 or ASCII with columns [E_loss, Intensity, Uncertainty]

experimental_functions: Pass detector output I(ΔE) to analysis workflow
Output directly interpretable RIXS spectrum for gap closure
experimental_components.notes: System F exists but is PASS-THROUGH. No transformation of observable. I(ΔE) from detector = I(ΔE) to observable.

physical_interactions.description: Undulator generates broad-spectrum soft X-rays, monochromator selects 853.4 eV

physical_interactions.physical_mechanism: X-ray absorption and RIXS excitation (Ni L3 edge resonance)
physical_interactions.interaction_strength: Flux at sample ~10^11-10^12 ph/s (after focusing losses)
physical_interactions.description: 853.4 eV X-rays excite Ni 2p → 3d transitions, creating excitons and other excitations

physical_interactions.interaction_strength: Thermal conductivity sets sample at T=40 K
physical_interactions.description: Cryostat cools sample to 40 K, ensuring antiferromagnetic order (TN=155 K)

physical_interactions.physical_mechanism: Resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) - Ni 2p3d excitations with energy loss
physical_interactions.interaction_strength: RIXS cross-section ~10^-26 cm^2 (typical), scattered intensity I(ΔE)

measured_data.exciton_dispersion: Maps as function of scattering angle (k-space)
measured_data.exciton_magnon_offset: ~1.4 eV (exciton appears 1.4 eV above double-magnon energy)
measured_data.spectral_width: ~100-200 meV FWHM (exciton lifetime broadening + instrumental resolution)

physical_interactions.description: THIS IS THE CRITICAL DATA - RIXS measures exciton energy loss of 1.47 eV. This encodes System D electronic properties.

physical_interactions.physical_mechanism: Pass-through (identity transformation) with minimal data reduction
physical_interactions.description: System F passes RIXS spectrum through without transformation. Energy calibration and normalization are applied, but the observable I(ΔE) is unchanged. This demonstrates that System F can be present even when no complex analysis is needed.

exciton_energy_loss.interpretation: Hund's exciton - electronic excitation where electron hops to neighboring Ni site with opposite spin

hund_exchange_interaction.interpretation: Energy offset between exciton and double-magnon, indicates Hund's exchange dominates exciton formation

exciton_dispersion.description: Exciton disperses through crystal with bandwidth ~100-200 meV

measured_observables: RIXS intensity I(ΔE) vs energy loss - shows peak at ΔE=1.47 eV
gap_closure_configuration.matrix_formulation: Infer System D (exciton energy) from measured D→E interaction (RIXS spectrum) given known A, B, C, E
gap_closure_configuration.expected_outcome: Gap closure should propose exciton energy ~1.47 eV and Hund's exchange ~1.4 eV

success_criteria.exciton_energy_match: Gap closure proposes exciton energy within 1.32-1.62 eV (±10% of 1.47 eV)
success_criteria.hund_exchange_match: Gap closure proposes Hund's exchange within 1.2-1.6 eV (±15% of 1.4 eV)

notes.validation_approach: This is a RIGOROUS TEST of Scientific Reflow. We are using real published data from a high-impact Nature Communications paper. If gap closure can successfully infer the exciton energy (~1.47 eV) from the experimental setup, it validates the framework.
notes.challenge: RIXS is a complex technique - the D→E interaction involves quantum mechanics (2p→3d transitions, exciton formation, inelastic scattering). The gap closure must capture that the 1.47 eV energy loss encodes System D electronic properties.
notes.realistic_expectations: We may not perfectly match 1.47 eV, but gap closure should: (1) Identify an excitation in the ~1-2 eV range, (2) Recognize it's related to electronic structure, (3) Provide a testable hypothesis. Even qualitative success (right order of magnitude) validates the approach.
notes.next_steps_after_this_test: If validation succeeds, we can refine Scientific Reflow with domain-specific physics (RIXS theory, exciton models). If it fails, we identify gaps in the framework (e.g., need better coupling between measurement matrix B and physical interactions).
